title: [CQ-I03a] Owned VM status and control CLI
description:
Objective: build the producer contract that CQ-I03 (JetBrains managed VM interface, task-63930ba4) and later CQ-I05 (VS Code) consume.

architect-4ae016fb split this out of I03 on 2026-10-29, following the human's 2026-10-27 instruction: "plan now instead of parking; if a prerequisite's contract must be designed first, split it out (SPIDR, as with R10a)". I03's earlier block named exactly this gap:
- scripts/local-runner/cli.mjs only offers doctor, prerequisites and native-smoke;
- R06's lifecycle.mjs (createLedger, reconcileOwned, cleanupOwned) has no IDE-callable entry point, and no ledger location.

Scope: host-side only, under scripts/local-runner/. No daemon tool, no IDE code, no activation.

Deliverable: scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs, with a CLI guarded by import.meta.url like cli.mjs:

`node scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs <status|reconcile|cleanup> --project <absolute path>`

It prints exactly ONE JSON line, at most 64 KiB, and exits 0 for every report; a refusal is a code inside the report. A usage error prints {"code":"VM_CONTROL_INPUT_INVALID"} and exits 2.

1. Ledger location: export ownedLedgerDir(projectPath).
   - It is <MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR (trimmed, resolved) | ~/.moe/runner-state>/<first 32 hex of sha256(canonical projectPath)>/vms, created with mode 0700.
   - It is never inside .moe/ or the repository, mirroring runnerKeyPath in packages/moe-daemon/src/server/runnerChannel.ts.
   - Canonicalize the project path the way the daemon names the project, so the IDE (D:/x), the ps1 wrapper (D:\x) and WSL (/mnt/d/x) reach the SAME ledger. Pin that with tests.
   - Activation (R11 final, V04b) must provision through this same ledger: say so in the header.
2. status returns {schema:'moe-vm-status-v1', provider:{ready, code?, platform?}, executionReady:false, verified:false, instances:[{instance, phase, state, launchTries, taskId}], invalid:<count>}:
   - provider comes from cli.mjs hostPrerequisites;
   - instances are ledger records ONLY. state comes from queryOwnedInstance on each record's own name, and is 'Unknown' on any failure;
   - a Multipass instance with no ledger record, moe-vm-* names included, is never listed.
3. reconcile returns R06's reconcileOwned report, with schema 'moe-vm-reconcile-v1'.
4. cleanup returns R06's cleanupOwned report, with schema 'moe-vm-cleanup-v1'.
   - attemptPhase and leaseHeld come from the DAEMON, never from arguments.
   - A record is deleted only when the daemon proves that its owner attempt is closed AND that the job lease jobLeaseResourceId(name) has no holder (moe.list_resources).
   - Anything unknown, superseded or unreachable is preserved, so it fails closed.
   - Reach the daemon over its existing loopback /mcp JSON-RPC path, as scripts/moe-call.sh does, or over the V04b1 runner channel if it has landed. If the existing projections (get_context view:'status' and its delivery attemptPhase) cannot prove 'closed' for the owner attempt, split out a read-only daemon slice instead of guessing.
5. No argument names, adds or adopts an instance: every control acts on the ledger alone.
6. executionReady and verified are always false. Nothing here claims isolation or enables verified-local.

Error handling: every failure is a fixed code. No path, stack, key or provider stderr reaches stdout.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs
definitionOfDone: status lists exactly the ledger's owned records and never a provider instance without a ledger record, and reports provider readiness separately from executionReady:false and verified:false, proven by scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs with fake provider, ledger and daemon.

reconcile and cleanup act only on ledger-owned names. cleanup deletes only a record whose owner attempt the daemon reports closed and whose job lease has no holder; it preserves every other, unknown or unreachable case, proven in the same file.

ownedLedgerDir resolves the same directory for Windows-drive, backslash and /mnt/<drive> spellings of one project, outside .moe/ and the repository. No argument can name, add or adopt an instance. Unknown subcommands or flags give VM_CONTROL_INPUT_INVALID with exit 2. Output is one JSON line of fixed codes with no path, stack, key or provider stderr.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
In scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs, add cleanup with daemon truth, plus the daemon caller. Report the file in modifiedFiles.

1. cleanupReport({ ledger, provider, call }):
   - list the ledger once, and build attemptId -> { taskId } from the records;
   - attemptPhase(attemptId): call('moe.get_context', { taskId }), the default view, which ends with servedContext.
     - servedContext.attemptId === attemptId gives 'running';
     - a served context whose attemptId differs or is absent gives 'closed'. The daemon keeps at most ONE open attempt per task and attempts are append-only (state/attemptStore.ts currentAttempt), so a ledger owner attempt that is not open is closed;
     - any refusal, malformed reply or transport failure gives 'unknown'.
   - leaseHeld(resourceId): one call('moe.list_resources', {}) per run, cached.
     - Adapt to its landed shape (state/resourceStore.ts): the resource is held iff its entry has a holder;
     - a resource not listed has no lease (false);
     - any failure gives true.
   - Then return { schema:'moe-vm-cleanup-v1', ...(await cleanupOwned({ ledger, provider, attemptPhase, leaseHeld })) }. R06's holdReason preserves anything not 'closed' or not lease-free.
2. The daemon caller, `export async function mcpCaller(projectPath, { WebSocketImpl = globalThis.WebSocket, timeoutMs = 15000 } = {})`:
   - readDaemonInfo reads <project>/.moe/daemon.json: at most MAX_DAEMON_INFO_BYTES (import it from guest-session.mjs) with a +1-byte read, a numeric port from 1 to 65535, a loopback host only (127.0.0.1 or ::1, or no bindHost), and a projectPath equal under canonicalProjectPath. Anything else rejects DAEMON_UNREACHABLE.
   - Open ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp. Each call sends one tools/call with a fresh id and resolves the parsed result.content[0].text JSON.
   - A JSON-RPC error rejects with its data.codeName.
   - A timeout, close or missing WebSocketImpl (Node < 22) rejects DAEMON_UNREACHABLE, so cleanup preserves everything.
   - The socket is closed in finally.

Error handling: no daemon reply text reaches the report beyond fixed codes. Make C1 and M1 pass.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN for C1, C1e and M1, plus the earlier L1, L2, S1 and R1 (7/10 in a /tmp snapshot; only runVmControl is stubbed).

cleanupReport:
- It lists the ledger once and hands cleanupOwned a ledger view whose list() returns that same listing. The attempt→task map and the cleanup therefore see identical records.
- attemptPhase calls get_context in its default view.
  - It gives 'running' when servedContext.attemptId equals the owner attempt. It gives 'closed' when it differs or is null.
  - It gives 'unknown' on a refusal, a malformed reply, a taskId mismatch, or receiptStatus 'identity-unreadable'. In that last case the daemon serves attemptId:null because the attempt could not be read; this is getContext.ts servedContextIdentity's decoded(), and it must not be read as 'closed'.
- leaseHeld makes one list_resources call, cached as a promise. It answers held iff the entry has holders; a resource that is not listed is free. A malformed list or a failed call counts as held.

mcpCaller and readDaemonInfo:
- readDaemonInfo uses O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, checks isFile, and reads at most MAX_DAEMON_INFO_BYTES+1 (imported from guest-session.mjs).
- It requires an integer port from 1 to 65535, a bindHost that is absent or 127.0.0.1/::1, and an equal canonical projectPath. Anything else gives DAEMON_UNREACHABLE, before any socket is opened.
- Each call opens one socket to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp. It rejects with the error's data.codeName, or DAEMON_REFUSED when there is none, and never carries the daemon's message text. A timeout, close, error or missing WebSocketImpl gives DAEMON_UNREACHABLE. The socket is closed in finally.

Note for I03: this project's live daemon.json has bindHost 0.0.0.0 (WSL agent mode). Under the plan's loopback-only rule, cleanup then preserves everything; that fails closed. I'll record it in the handoff.

GREEN: all 8 rows pass in the shared tree (`node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs`).

CLI:
- runVmControl(argv, {write, provider, ...deps}) accepts exactly 3 argv entries: a subcommand in {status, reconcile, cleanup}, the literal '--project', and an absolute path with no control characters.
- Anything else prints '{"code":"VM_CONTROL_INPUT_INVALID"}\n' and exits 2, before any dependency is read. C2 and U1 prove this with throwing spies.
- Real deps: createLedger(ownedLedgerDir(project)), provider {} (multipass), cli.mjs hostPrerequisites, and mcpCaller(project) for cleanup only.
- A report of 64 KiB or more becomes VM_CONTROL_REPORT_TOO_LARGE. Any throw becomes VM_CONTROL_FAILED with exit 0, and nothing is written to stderr.
- main is guarded by import.meta.url, as in cli.mjs. The subprocess rows in U1 (exit 2) and O1 (exit 0, exact bytes) prove the guard.

Size: the plan's row matrix put me at 485 lines, so I trimmed to fit the 400 cap without dropping any case. To save lines:
- L2 is merged into L1, and C1e into C1;
- C2 and U1 share a refusedUntouched helper;

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW done (my own diff: vm-control.mjs, its test, cli.mjs export).

FIXED, real risk: list_resources was cached for the whole run. cleanupOwned deletes sequentially, each delete taking up to 120 s, so a later record's lease decision could be minutes stale, and a VM a job leased mid-run could have been deleted. The lease is now read fresh for each closed record, just before its delete. C1 asserts the exact call interleaving [gc, gc, lr, gc, lr, gc, lr, gc, gc, gc]. A cache mutant fails C1. A full re-sweep on the final source killed 36/36, and the shared tree matches the snapshot by sha.

Considered and safe:
- Foreign moe-vm-* names with no record are never queried (S1). A tampered record fails validRecord/isOwnedInstanceName and is only counted in invalid.
- An open owner attempt gives attempt-active. After a daemon restart the attempts are reconciling, which is in OPEN_PHASES, so currentAttempt serves them and they are preserved.
- identity-unreadable, or an attemptId that is neither a string nor null, gives unknown.
- A non-loopback bindHost, another project's daemon.json (canonical projectPath) or an oversized file is refused before any socket opens.
- No argv echo. Only fixed codes and validated names, phases and task ids reach stdout; provider and daemon text never does; stderr is empty.
- Socket, timer and file handle are closed on every path.
- Two concurrent cleanups: R06's CAS makes the second one LEDGER_CONFLICT, which is harmless.

Residuals, documented (header and handoff):
- the lease race between the fresh read and the delete (seconds);
- a malformed attempt file dropped by the daemon's loadEntities looks closed, and only the lease check guards it;
- a stale daemon.json port reused by a hostile local process that speaks JSON-RPC;
- WSL mode (bindHost 0.0.0.0) always preserves;
- UNC paths do not match across OSes (unsupported, as in the proxy). The inside-project guard only checks '/' separators, so it is ineffective for UNC;
- status lists collision and deleted records, which I03 must render as foreign or filter out.

Rails: daemon.json is only read; no .moe writes, no Git writes, no forbidden tokens. executionReady and verified are false, and nothing is activated.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A new read-only daemon tool for the attempt phase: unnecessary. The daemon keeps at most one open attempt per task (attemptStore currentAttempt), and attempts are append-only. So get_context's servedContext, which names the open attempt, proves that a ledger owner attempt is closed when it is not that attempt. A refusal or failure gives 'unknown', which preserves the VM.
- Spawning moe-proxy as moe-call.sh does: heavier, and it needs the proxy dist. A dependency-free /mcp WebSocket caller (Node 22+ global WebSocket) is about 30 lines; on older Node it fails closed.
- Listing provider instances: rejected. Ownership is the ledger only, and status queries each ledger name individually.
- Editing ci.yml: deferred to CQ-I06, because V04b1 and V04b, both unlanded, hold it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Verified:
- lifecycle.mjs exports createLedger(stateDir).list() → {records, invalid}, queryOwnedInstance, reconcileOwned, cleanupOwned({ledger, provider, attemptPhase, leaseHeld}) and isOwnedInstanceName. Owner records carry {taskId, attemptId, generation}. jobLeaseResourceId(name) gives the lease id.
- cli.mjs: hostPrerequisites is module-private; runCli(argv, { write }) is exported.
- guest-session.mjs exports MAX_DAEMON_INFO_BYTES (16384).
- packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts comparableProjectPath is the D:\ vs /mnt/d rule.
- runnerChannel.ts runnerKeyPath is the precedent for a per-project hash location.
- ExecutionAttemptPhase is running | finalizing | reconciling | closed. currentAttempt returns the open one or null.
- get_context's default read ends with servedContext {attemptId, generation} of the open attempt.
- ci.yml's 'Test local runner prerequisite bundles' step lists test files explicitly.
planningNotes.risks:
- Lease race: a lease granted between list_resources and delete. The mutex is daemon-side, and this CLI is not atomic with it. Document it as a residual. R10's job flow acquires before use and the VM name is random, so the window is narrow; never retry a delete.
- Node < 22 has no global WebSocket, so cleanup preserves everything (DAEMON_UNREACHABLE). Document it.
- list_resources' landed shape: adapt, and fail closed on anything unreadable.
- Size: keep the module to about 170 lines and the test to about 220, within the 400-net cap.
- Windows: L1's win32 rows. Run once on Windows node if available.
- No VM is created here, and no isolation is claimed.

completionSummary:
CQ-I03a delivered: scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs (new, 182 lines), scripts/tests/local-runner-vm-control.test.mjs (new, 215 lines), and one word in cli.mjs (`export` on hostPrerequisites, +1/-1). That is 398 added lines, at most 400.

CLI: `vm-control.mjs <status|reconcile|cleanup> --project <abs>` takes exactly 3 argv entries and prints one JSON line under 64 KiB, exiting 0. Schemas are moe-vm-{status,reconcile,cleanup}-v1. Any other argv gives VM_CONTROL_INPUT_INVALID with exit 2, before anything is read. Other codes: VM_CONTROL_FAILED, VM_CONTROL_REPORT_TOO_LARGE, LEDGER_UNREADABLE. stderr is always empty.

- ownedLedgerDir is <MOE_RUNNER_STATE_DIR | ~/.moe/runner-state>/sha256(canonical)[:32]/vms, created 0700, and is refused if it resolves inside the project. D:/, D:\ and /mnt/d spellings reach one directory.
- status lists ledger records only, each queried by its own name; state is 'Unknown' or 'Absent' when the query fails or finds nothing. Provider readiness is separate, and executionReady and verified are always false.
- cleanup:
  - Owner attempt closed: servedContext.attemptId differs from it or is null. identity-unreadable or malformed gives unknown.
  - Lease free: a fresh list_resources read per record, held iff it has holders. A record not listed is free; a failure counts as held.
  - The daemon is reached over loopback /mcp. daemon.json must be bounded, loopback, and for the same project. Node 22+ WebSocket is required; otherwise everything is preserved.

Deviations:
- `invalid` is a count in every report: ledger file names are not fixed codes.
- There is one fresh lease read per record, not a per-run cache. Adversarial review found a cache would go stale across 120 s deletes.

- Also 8/8 on Windows Node 24.16 and on Node 18/20/22.
